It is a focus and success talisman used in meditation to enhance creativity and sharpen the mind. The Neolithic era in Europe began using amethyst as early as 25,000 B.C. Its spiritual and mystical energies made it a popular material for beads and amulets in numerous cultures. Later, it was used in crowns, scepters, and jewelry as a royal stone and considered as one of the most precious stones in the world alongside rubies, sapphires, emeralds and diamonds until the 18th century.

Amethyst Buying Guide

Check its Origin:

Amethyst is found on several continents and in particular in India, Madagascar, Namibia and Tanzania. But the best, finest and most sought after amethysts are those of the South American continent, particularly those sourced from Brazil and Uruguay.

Observe their Color:

Amethyst crystal color quality ranges from extremely pale to intense or very dark purple hue. The darker the amethyst, the higher it is prized on this range, unless it is so dark that it appears black in low light. In fact, the ideal color is known as Siberian purple, after the region where the deepest purple stones can be found. Whatever darker is the purple hue, look for uniform color and tone.

When viewing a natural Amethyst gemstone, zone lines can be seen in the gemstone. When the heat of the Earth causes color differences as it rises to the surface, these lines form, and indicates its authenticity. On a fake amethyst stone, these lines will not be as defined and distinct as they would be on a genuine one.

Notice their Clarity:

An amethyst with a light hue and high clarity is an attractive gemstone for jewelry. For these gems to be valuable, however, they must look much neater than the darker gems. Amethysts are valued based on the way neat or clean from inclusions and shades they appear, not how neat or clean they actually are. For this reason, most amethysts are deep purple. Regardless of clarity, all amethyst gemstones lighten to their lightest natural hues when exposed to direct sunlight.

Examine their Inclusions:

The majority of faceted amethyst on the market is eye-clean, indicating it lacks inclusions visible to the naked eye. African sourced gemstones, particularly from Zambia, can be an intense raspberry hue. It typically contains more inclusions than gemstones from Brazil. However, due to its exceptional color, this is acceptable for a faceted gemstone. Amethyst of the same hue that is free of flaws is more valuable. Amethysts with visible inclusions but an attractive color are typically fashioned into cabochons or beads. Rarely is amethyst treated to fill surface-reaching fractures in order to improve its apparent clarity.

See their Shape:

Raw Amethyst clusters are carved into numerous standard shapes and designs, including rounds, ovals, pears, emerald cuts, triangles, marquises, and cushions, among others. Amethyst is also a popular gemstone for sculpting into a variety of freeform shapes. They occasionally exhibit concave shapes, where normally flat faces are concave. There are also other types of cuts and carvings, such as animal and object cuttings.

Check the Carats:

For Amethyst of gem quality, the raw Amethyst is divided and polished into smaller stones of variable carat weight. In general, Amethyst weighing between 5 and 7 carats are appropriate for jewelry. Because Amethyst is sold by weight, Amethyst prices are calculated per carat. Stones of comparable dimensions but distinct varieties vary greatly in price. The more carats and clarity Amethyst has, the higher its price.

Avoid Heated & Treated Amethyst

Due to treatments the Amethyst stone loses its natural composition and thus loses its natural frequency. These heated and treated Amethyst do not offer any healing benefits and should be avoided.

Check for Lab Certificate

It is recommended that you should purchase Amethyst gemstones along a lab tested certificate which can determine its authenticity, treatment status and origin. Rudra Centre has been dealing in natural unheated untreated lab certified gemstones for the past 25 years. Our Amethyst are certified from trusted labs like GIA, IGI, GLI and IGITL.

Why buy Amethyst from Rudra Centre?

We only deal with untreated and unheated gemstones from their natural sources, which we energize in accordance with Vedic Vidhi, after more than 20 years of research and 100.000+ satisfied, healed, and empowered customers.

Can I give my used Amethyst gemstone to someone else?

You should avoid it if you are wearing it. However, if you have not used it for an extended period, you can pass it on to someone else. It is recommended to not wear it for at least 2 weeks before giving it to someone else. You can also follow the cleansing and reenergizing process mentioned in the benefits section.

For the best results it is highly recommended that one wears only 100% natural, unheated, and untreated Amethyst gemstones. As per the Vedic scriptures, a heat treatment harms its sattvic nature, rendering the stone less effective and beneficial. Like other gemstones, the quality of Amethyst is also determined by the four Cs (Color, Cut, Carat, Clarity). 

Color

The color of the finest amethyst is an intense reddish purple or violet with no apparent color zoning. As long as the stone is not so dark as to diminish its brilliance, dealers prefer intensely saturated reddish-purple to dark purple. Under dim lighting conditions, if the color is too dark, an amethyst may appear black.

Cut

Amethysts are commonly faceted or cabochon-shaped stones. The process of dividing a gemstone into numerous small, flat surfaces known as facets is known as faceting. Each of these facets reflects light, increasing the brightness. Faceting also allows you to see all sides of an amethyst without having to rotate it too much.

Carat

Amethyst of 10 – 30 carat is most popular in Vedic Astrology. Significant smaller and larger Amethyst are used in contemporary jewelry. Generally, the price of Amethyst rises as the size/weight/carat increases.

Clarity

Best quality amethyst gemstones have total clarity and are totally translucid under direct sunlight exposure. Amethyst is a naturally very abundant and pure gemstone. It shows few or no inclusions to the naked eye.

Dealers deal in Amethyst stones which are synthetic to natural but which are treated/heated and color enhanced, so it is immensely important to purchase only from a reputed dealer with certification from a reputed lab.

Amethyst Gemstone Price

Amethyst stone price is determined by its size, cut, and origin in terms of color and clarity. Cabochons and beads with fine tones and transparency command a premium price. However, because amethyst is found in abundance on all continents, the price of amethyst gemstone is considered low when looking to buy amethyst stone online. The deeper the purple color, the higher its price.

When a gemstone is heat-treated or undergoes the dying process, its healing properties are lost when it is worn. Amethyst has numerous curative properties; to maximize its curative effects, only untreated Amethyst stone should be worn. Large sizes of amethyst are not significantly more expensive per carat than smaller sizes, making it an excellent choice for bold jewelry designs.

Amethyst crystal price of genuine, natural and unheated, untreated Amethyst at Rudra Centre ranges from INR 700 to INR 49,300 (USD 8.75 to USD 616) depending on their Carats. The average price for the required standard carats is INR 6,000 (USD 75).

How to Identify or Test Original & Authentic Amethyst?

The best way to check the authenticity of Amethyst is by getting a Lab tested report from a reputed laboratory. Rudra Centre only deals with Vedic Astrology approved gemstones that are natural, untreated, and unheated. All our Amethyst are certified by reputable labs like GIA, GLI, IGI and IGITL.

Look for flaws along with inclusions. Use a magnifying glass with at least 10x magnification to examine the Amethyst carefully. Look for specks and blemishes, as they form with minute particles of other material. These flaws are strong evidence that Amethyst is genuine. Lab-created (fake) Amethyst have no inclusions of this nature, and neither do natural Amethyst, but if you find flaws, then your Amethyst is genuine.

Examine the gemstone for air bubbles. Essentially, lab-created Amethyst is glass that has undergone a process similar to that which forms natural Amethyst. Since they are made of glass, they retain miniscule air bubbles after formation. If there are bubbles within the Amethyst, it is not genuine. Be sure to inspect your Amethyst from every angle by turning it over. There is a possibility that bubbles of air will only be evident from a single angle.

Look at how light is reflected by the Amethyst. Turn off all the lights and shine your flashlight on the Amethyst. If it is genuine, it will only reflect light of the same hue as itself. If it is a fake, made of glass, it will reflect colors other than the natural color of the gem.

Amethyst Cleaning & Maintenance

It is essential to give your gemstone a thorough cleaning in order to preserve its luster, as regular use can cause it to become dull. This washing enables it to purge itself from negative energies as well.

Amethyst crystal in particular is critical to look after its cleanliness and maintenance since it has important and numerous medical and healing properties. Therefore, washing with warm water and gentle cleansers would have been ideal. If necessary, utilize a brush and a soft towel to complete the cleaning process.

Ultrasonic cleaners are generally safe, with the exception of stones that have been dyed or filled with fracture filler. Amethyst should not be cleaned with steam or exposed to high temperatures.
